phase_one:
Use case: game-sprite-sheet.
Create a production pixel-art sprite atlas for a Godot 2D side-scrolling Minecraft-inspired game: the mine boss "Riftstone Ravager". ONE transparent PNG, preferred canvas 1536x2048, exactly 3 columns by 8 rows, 24 distinct full-body frames. Every invisible cell is the same size. No text, labels, grid lines, border, scenery, ground, shadows, detached particles or extra actors. Genuine transparent alpha background, not a black background or a checkerboard baked into the pixels. Leave generous transparent gutters around every frame.

Character: unmistakable Minecraft ravager-inspired giant blocky quadruped. Bulky rectangular slate-gray stone-skinned torso, big square illager-like head and long broad rectangular nose, heavy brow, small pale eyes, a pair of thick short ivory curved horns, four heavy cuboid legs with dark hooves, charcoal iron shoulder/back plates, dark brown leather harness and small iron studs. Minecraft proportions but polished handcrafted 16-bit pixel illustration, dark crisp stepped outlines, controlled slate blue/gray palette, small warm highlights. No rider, no axe, no weapon in its mouth, no rhino nose-horn. Opaque solid character. Flat readable pixel shading, sharp edges and deliberate pixels, no painterly blur.

All 24 frames show the EXACT SAME individual, side-profile facing RIGHT, same camera, constant scale and character proportions. Consistent full-body silhouette, approximately 360 pixels wide and 190 pixels tall inside each 512x256 cell, hooves at the same baseline 230px down the cell. All horns/tail/feet contained inside their own cells. Keep body center horizontally aligned, no camera zoom or perspective shifts. STRICT orthographic horizontal platform-game view, not an isometric sprite. Pose movement is local, never crosses a cell boundary.

Read each row left to right as three successive animation keyframes:
Row 1: three idle breathing frames, neutral standing, slight chest rise and head motion.
Row 2: three walk-cycle frames, alternate front/rear legs clearly, big heavy footsteps.
Row 3: three charge preparation frames: scrape a front hoof, crouch shoulders, then lower head with horns aimed forward.
Row 4: three running charge frames: body low, head forward, legs in distinct galloping poses.
Row 5: three horn attack frames: pull head back/up, wind up, then a decisive horizontal horn thrust to the RIGHT.
Row 6: three ground-stomp frames: lift front feet, rear higher before impact, then slam both forefeet down while lowering shoulders.
Row 7: three stunned/hit frames: slack lowered head and bent knees, tilted head, then recover posture; no stars drawn, effects added in engine.
Row 8: three death frames: knees buckle, heavy body falls sideways, then lies completely flat with closed eyes, all feet/horns remain visible. Keep corpse at the same floor baseline.

This must look like a cohesive actual animated sprite atlas rather than a concept-art page. Animate limbs and head between frames; do not repeat one pose in every cell. No second-phase orange cracks yet.
phase_two:
Edit this sprite atlas into the SECOND PHASE of the SAME Riftstone Ravager boss. Preserve the transparent background, exactly 3 columns by 8 rows, all 24 corresponding animation poses, their locations, scales, facing RIGHT, feet baselines, proportions, horns, harness, outlines and empty gutters. Do not rearrange, remove or add frames.
Change only the armor/skin phase appearance: charcoal iron plates visibly fractured with angular bright amber/orange pixel cracks through the shoulder and back plates; a few small gaps between chipped plates reveal ember-orange light, warmer dark gray underlying skin, glowing amber eyes. Horns stay ivory and harness stays dark brown. Give all 24 frames the same second-phase design, including the three collapsed/death frames in the bottom row (death eyes closed, cracks dimmer).
Keep the crisp stepped pixel-art shading and clear heavy blocky side-view silhouette. No big flame aura, no particles outside the silhouette, no blurred glow, no scenery, no text, no checkerboard texture. The first atlas is the edit target, not a loose style reference. Keep exact existing cell layout and shapes so the same game frame indices remain valid. Genuine transparent alpha outside each sprite.
